draft.title: Gradient-intercept form
card: A straight line can be written as \(y = mx + c\). This is called gradient-intercept form.
Gradient
\(m\) is the number multiplying \(x\). It tells you how much \(y\) changes when \(x\) goes up by 1. A negative \(m\) means the line slopes down.
y-intercept
\(c\) is the number added on its own. It is the value of \(y\) where the line crosses the y-axis, at the point \((0, c)\).
Example
For \(y = 2x - 3\), \(m = 2\) and \(c = -3\). Start at \((0, -3)\). Go across 1 and up 2 to reach \((1, -1)\). Join the points with a line.

4.alt: The line \(y = 2x - 3\), crossing the y-axis at \((0, -3)\) and passing through \((1, -1)\) and \((2, 1)\).

draft.remember: In \(y = mx + c\), \(m\) is the gradient and \(c\) is where the line meets the y-axis.

a.q: What are the gradient and y-intercept of the line \(y = -4x + 5\)?
a.why: The number multiplying \(x\) is the gradient, \(-4\). The number added on its own is the y-intercept, \(5\). Swapping the two is a common mistake, but \(c\) is the part without \(x\).
a.clue: The gradient is the number multiplying \(x\), with its sign.

b.q: Priya draws the line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 3\). She starts at the y-intercept. Which move takes her to another point on the line?
b.why: The y-intercept is \((0, 3)\) and the gradient is \(-\frac{1}{2}\). So \(y\) falls 1 each time \(x\) rises 2, which gives \((2, 2)\). Across 2 and up 1 would give a gradient of \(\frac{1}{2}\), which slopes up.
b.clue: Start at \((0, 3)\). A negative gradient means the line goes down as it goes right.
